title: UI design: hierarchy and colour
goal: Create a clear visual hierarchy with reusable styles.
explanation: Visual hierarchy guides attention. Give the page one clear primary action, group related controls, and leave enough space between unrelated sections.
Use a small type scale, a consistent spacing scale and reusable colour tokens. Colour can reinforce meaning, but labels and icons must also communicate important states.
Check contrast rather than judging by appearance. Make interactive elements look interactive, and provide visible hover, focus, disabled and error states.
exercise: Design a contact card with a title, helpful text and one primary button. Explain why the button gets visual emphasis.
hint: Start with hierarchy and spacing before adding decoration.

quiz.question: Which design communicates an error most reliably?
options: A red border plus an explanatory text message
quiz.explanation: Text explains the problem even when colour or motion is not perceived.
